utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's discuss the meeting you had with the judge. When you were interviewed by this investigative judge, was this meeting, or however you want to describe it, held in a courtroom?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "a room," do you mean an office or just an empty room? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some kind of an office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any witnesses called to testify against you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you call any witnesses to testify on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if there were no witnesses, was a trial held?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I was sentenced to 12 years in prison, but as to how the trial was carried out, and on what basis, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were sentenced, you were returned to Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you leave Batkovici? What month and year?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of June, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at Batkovici, from November 1992 to June 9th, 1994, did you ever see any of the defendants at that prison camp?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see Miroslav Tadic on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you first saw Miroslav Tadic at Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In January 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on these several times that Miroslav Tadic visited Batkovici, what did he do?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came in with the lists of people for the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when he came there with those lists of persons or prisoners to be exchanged, who read out those names?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes he would read them and sometimes the guards did, but in most cases he himself read them out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he read them, did he make any racial slurs to you, towards you, at Batkovici?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him saying anything in Batkovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it that he called the prisoners balijas and Ustasha?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the elementary school in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let us move to the process of announcing or calling out the names. If a person's name was called, what would happen to that person? Would they leave immediately? Did they leave the next day? Did he go with Miroslav Tadic? What would happen?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In most cases, they would go with him to the buses and then they would go to Samac, spend a night there, and then they would be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you previously testified that during the summer of 1992, when a person's name was called out to be exchanged, he received a final beating from the guards. At Batkovici, did anything happen to the prisoners after their name was called out for an exchange?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in Batkovici. There was no abuse there. When the names were read out, the names of the people to be exchanged, they were not maltreated in Batkovici. But I heard that when they were taken to Bosanski Samac to spend a night there, that they were maltreated there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's return to the process of announcing the names. Were there ever occasions when a person's name was called but that the person was not present, they were out doing forced labour or they were somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On several occasions, people were out on forced labour. They simply were not there when Tadic came in with the lists of people to be exchanged. And then other people would be put on those lists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us: What would happen prior to other people's names being placed on the list to replace those that were not there when the names were called out?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tadic came into the camp. He read out the names. If somebody was absent -- we would always gather around him. Some people who had money would give him money, and then he would go out and came back in with the amended list and read out their names as people to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when a person -- so if a person was not present, replacements would be added. Now, you said people would give Tadic money to become those replacements. Did you ever witness any prisoner giving the defendant Miroslav Tadic any money?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on those several occasions where prisoners bribed Miroslav Tadic, were their names added to the exchange list?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those people released and exchanged that same day or on the following day?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on the same day, that they went on the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names or can you recall the names of prisoners that bribed Miroslav Tadic to have their names placed on the exchange list?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion I was there when Sabah Seric paid Miroslav Tadic to be exchanged, and he went. I saw some other people too, but I don't recall their names. Most of them were Catholics from the Samac municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Sabah Seric bribe Miroslav Tadic just for himself, or for others to be exchanged also?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He tried to bribe him for another man too, but Tadic didn't agree; he refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he accept the money first and then refuse, or did he refuse prior to accepting the money?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember how it was exactly. I don't think that he accepted money from this other man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, prior to Miroslav Tadic's visits to Batkovici, was there any discussion among the prisoners concerning bribing Miroslav Tadic to get your name placed on the exchange list?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was talk. Those who had money knew that they could give the money to Miroslav Tadic to get out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were in Batkovici during 1993 and 1994. During what years did this occur? And when I say "this occur," the bribes to Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever offer Miroslav Tadic a bribe?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't, because I didn't have any money.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you remained in prison until June 1994?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just a few other questions relating to Miroslav Tadic. When you saw him at Batkovici, had his appearance changed, his facial appearance?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had a long beard. I don't remember exactly, but I do know that he had a very big beard. I don't remember any other changes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, speaking of exchanges, were any members -- just first yes or no: Were any members of your family exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's begin with your wife and daughter. When were they exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In October 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were they exchanged to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in Dragalic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether any of the defendants were present at that exchange?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife told me that Miroslav Tadic was present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your mother, was she exchanged out of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when she was exchanged from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in June or July 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know -- where did she go, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the exchange took place in the same place, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dragalic. Do you know whether any of the defendants were present at your mother's exchange in June or July of 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My mother told me that Miroslav Tadic had been there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony, you mentioned your grandparents living in Bosanski Samac. Were either of your grandparents exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to your grandmother?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My grandmother died in December 1993, and my grandfather fled from Samac in 1994, in September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us why your grandfather fled Bosanski Samac in September?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came there, he told us that some Serbs had come and had told him that he had to leave the house, to move out, that they needed the house, and he had no other choice but to flee Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had your grandfather lived in that house that he was told that he had to vacate?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 50 years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this happen just to your grandfather in September, or was anyone else told that they had to vacate their homes at that time?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My neighbours from across, a family -- there was a Catholic family -- in fact, just the man was Catholic. They also had to leave their house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this just one neighbour or several neighbours?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three neighbours, three persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of what ethnic group were these three persons? Were they all Catholic Croatians or were they of various ethnic backgrounds?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The husband and wife were Catholic, and the third person was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And persons of what ethnic group told them that they had to vacate their homes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your grandfather and those neighbours do anything as a result of being told that they had to vacate their homes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They did nothing. They simply fled Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during what month did they flee Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when were you exchanged? You said in June of 1994?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were exchanged with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were 12 of us prisoners and some 150 civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was exchanged in Satorovici. That's a village near Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's within the state of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go after you were exchanged?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Slavonia, where my wife and children were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the time of your exchange, what physical injuries were you suffering?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had three broken ribs, my teeth were knocked out, I had difficulties in eating and with sleeping, I was quite tense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the problem that you had with eating last?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About three months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of these physical problems exist prior to your imprisonment in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if any, emotional problems did you have upon being exchanged in June of 1994? You indicated that you had some problems sleeping. What other emotional problems did you suffer?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm quite tense, and I can't spend a lot of time in one place in a closed environment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other emotional problems that you've suffered?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to being imprisoned in 1992, did you suffer these same problems?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the beginning of your testimony, you mentioned that your family had three homes: Your uncle's home, your mother's home, which was on the same place of land or in a little complex, and else where you had an apartment. What happened to these three homes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of that was confiscated. We have nothing any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is anyone living in those three homes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody lives in my uncle's house. As for the rest, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your uncle ever give anyone permission to move into his home?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was rent ever paid to your uncle for living -- for the right to live in his home?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has your uncle made any attempt to get his property back?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has he retained counsel to try and get his property back?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did. Yes, in fact he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did he retain counsel to try and get his property back?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he went there two years ago, and he paid some money -- I don't know how much -- to the attorney, in order for him to fix the papers for the house.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the name of the attorney.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, what's the name of the attorney, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Boro Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the past two years since he's retained counsel, has he received his property back?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing has happened yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many years had that piece of property been in your uncle's family?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly, but I think for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have you taken any action or has your mother taken any action to get your homes back?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we have not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why is that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Why would I have to pay to somebody for something that has been confiscated and stolen from me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, about three to four months after you were exchanged, did you do something?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you join a military group?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was a member of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you serve in the HVO army?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the place or the armed formation?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both. In what capacity did you serve and where?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Domaljevac, and I was in reconnaissance sabotage unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did you serve in the HVO army?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately one year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you previously indicated that your mother's family had lived in Bosanski Samac for generations. In April, prior to the war, did you have any intention of leaving the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your relatives have any intention or want to leave the town of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they did not, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you and everyone else leave, all the members of your family? Why?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't leave; we were expelled from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if not for the beatings, the imprisonment, and the persecution, would you have left Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just a moment. I have to organise my papers. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Subasic. My name is Pantelic, and I am the attorney of Blagoje Simic. Now that you have mentioned that you were a member of the HVO unit in the region of Domaljevac, these operations that you were involved in were probably in the front that was in Grebnice region; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yes, but the interpreters did not translate that.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said "yes." The interpreter probably didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you hear the interpreter now? Let's make a test. Is everything functioning well? [In English] Can you hear the translator? Can you hear the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hear and understand Mr. Pantelic well, or perhaps I should be -- I should speak in English so that we can understand each other better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. Subasic. Your answer was not recorded, so I thought there was a problem with interpretation. But let's continue. Can you tell me what was the name of this HVO unit that you were a member of.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 104th Bosanski Samac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of this 104th HVO Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the name. It's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What rank did you hold in the 104th HVO Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Just a minute. The registrar needs to say something.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, since you are speaking the same language as the witness, you started your question before the witness was finished answering. Pause a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think, Mr. Pantelic, you should speak up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, I will take care about the ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, do you have any information regarding the fact that according to the Dayton Peace Accords, all citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, regardless of their ethnicity, have a guaranteed right to return of their property?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. And are you aware of how much this return of the property can cost when you have to pay the attorney? You know that better than I do, because you are in the field in Bosnia, so you should be well aware of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, you are there to answer questions from counsel and you're not supposed to ask him any questions. So just answer questions put to you by counsel. We shall move much faster.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, I'm asking you now whether you or your mother have initiated the procedure for return of your property, just like your uncle did, by engaging a local attorney.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we have not done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will have a couple of questions with regard to the witness's -- among these witnesses certain number are protected, so I would kindly ask to go into private session because of the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What do you mean? The questions involve witnesses who are protected?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. All right. Can we go into private session, then?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Subasic, you are telling us that you and these people that we have mentioned simply discussed private matters and never, ever said a word about their testimonies here and what they testified about here. Is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I said I discussed anything with these people. I simply said that I saw these people, and that doesn't necessarily mean that I discussed anything with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before these people went to testify here, did you, before that, talk and reminisce about the events that took place in Samac ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. I don't know whether you are aware of the reason why I didn't go to The Hague. I had an accident at work. I broke both of my arms, I had a back injury, and was therefore unable to travel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was the last time you talked to Esad Dagovic?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a year ago, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in the HVO brigade with you after he was exchanged, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I haven't seen Esad Dagovic since 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what other people from Samac served in that HVO brigade with you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't like to mention any names. I don't think that's important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: When you talked to Esad Dagovic, did you discuss the statements that you had given to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not talk about that. We had not seen each other for a long time and did not even consider discussing these matters. We talked about private affairs, about his marriage and the fact that he was supposed to come for his vacation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, is it appropriate time for a break now? Because I'm going to another line of questioning. Or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. We shall take our break now for 20 minutes and continue the proceedings at 1750 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Cross-examination continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Subasic, please tell me: This apartment that you lived in in Samac, your mother helped you obtain that apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't get that apartment. That was an apartment owned by my mother, and I merely lived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She got that apartment from her company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did she get that apartment, then?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She got it from the Veterans' Association.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But how? Why did she get it from the Veterans' Association? She was not a veteran fighter, was she?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Her father was, and she got it as a child of a veteran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So she had a contract entitling her to use the apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how it was. We moved into that apartment in December 1991, and the war broke out in Samac in 1992, in April. So we were not able by that time to get all the papers in order for the apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we," who do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean myself and my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to some information from Samac, you and your mother moved into that apartment forcibly. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a way, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you probably know that you cannot seek the return of the property if there is no legal owner of the property and if there is no proof of ownership. You are aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that, and I already said that I didn't seek anything; I didn't apply for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was why -- that was because there was no legal basis for the use of the apartment?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was legal basis for the use, but I was unable to get all the papers in order, and I didn't want to do anything in that respect. But I'm sure that once I am willing to do so, I will be able to fix everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked in the Mebos company. That's a company that manufactured electrical appliances, water heaters and things like that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You worked in the production line in that company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the search of your apartment, some wires were found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of wires were they?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just ordinary wires used for fitting the water heaters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had brought these from the factory; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had bought them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you constructed water heaters in your apartment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you buy the wires?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fixed water heaters for other people in the apartment -- in other people's apartments.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also fitted thermostats in water heaters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. If it was necessary, I did so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the inspector in the police asked you whether you had constructed some kind of sabotage, booby traps, and other types of explosive devices because the wires that had been found in your apartment, what did you say to Milos Savic in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have no copy of any statement that this witness made Milos Savic, and he just -- and counsel just asked a question in relation to what Milos Savic asked this witness. If they have a copy of these statements, I would ask that it be provided to us immediately. That never came out on direct, that question there, so if they have a copy of the statement, I'd ask that it be provided to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No statement, Your Honour. Obviously, if we would be in possession of such a document, we would deliver that immediately to the Prosecution. It's simply an information from the field about the background of certain events around this witness, so I'm going to explore this area to check what is actually true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He said -- he made an indication "when the inspector asked you," and once again, if they have any proof or indication, other than -- if all he has is some information he's heard, then he should ask it in a different manner. He's asking it as if it did in fact happen. He can ask if they did ask you that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's the way that the question has been phrased that is the problem. Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You've understood what Mr. Weiner is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Subasic, you will agree with the claim that there were grounds for suspicion on the part of the police that you were engaged in subversive activities and that is why you were arrested; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But since you were a member of the sabotage unit in 104th Brigade of the HVO, you were, in a way, an expert for subversive activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection. He was a member of that unit almost two and a half or two and a quarter years after the search of his home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is after his exchange?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Correct. Three months later he then joins the unit. You can't base his activities two and a quarter years or 27 months earlier based on what he did later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think there is a basis for that, because if the person has technical or personal knowledge of certain items, equipment, booby traps, he can use his personal knowledge while in the combat operations. So, for example --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think you've understood. The objection is that he joined this 104th Brigade after his release, three months after he was exchanged, in 1994, and your question is based on his arrest in 1992, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct. I want to make a link between these two periods of time, and that's the basis of my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you first ask him whether he was engaged in such activities in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Mr. Subasic, you performed certain subversive activities for the SDA, the armed forces of the SDA in Samac, in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not a member of any party in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did have the requisite knowledge to make timed explosive devices; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have the requisite knowledge to turn a water heater into an explosive device?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what kind of knowledge did you have that qualified you to be in the sabotage unit of the 104th HVO Brigade in 1994? Did you make any kind of sabotage devices there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he was a member of it's either the sabotage and reconnaissance or the reconnaissance and sabotage unit. No one's even brought out what he did within that unit to even take it to that next level. They're trying to leave an inference that because he was in that unit, he was definitely in the sabotage side of it. If you'd like to question him what he did in that unit, maybe it would be enlightening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. I think there is a problem with mixing the information and not directing the questions to the activities of the witness at the relevant period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, in any case, Your Honour, since it's a little bit in war period, it's quite suspicious activity that someone has this equipment and wires and the thermostat in his apartment. Probably for the police members he was simply suspicious doing certain equipment, and then they arrested him and tried to explain --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. No one --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was my basis of the questions, so I just try to explore this issue, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think you have done that sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm really sorry, but when you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You wanted to say something?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you said that the police found the thermostat and wire in my apartment, I never mentioned that the police had found the thermostat, They only found the wire. For me, it was so insignificant. Any of us would have a piece of wire in their homes, perhaps several metres of wire. You would use it to install the speakers or to change the wire in the water heater, but thermostats were never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Pantelic, you can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but in 1992, did they suspect you of making such explosive devices? Did they accuse you of it? The police, did they do so?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they accused each of us of something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that was not my question. My question referred to you. Can you tell us: What did the police accuse you of?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they came to take me with them, they told me that I would only have to make a statement, and then when I came there, they asked me about the wire, and the other questions were how many Serbs I had killed, how many women I had killed by slitting their throats, how many women I had raped. So the wire was mentioned as an aside. In the whole course of my imprisonment, nobody ever mentioned the wire at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but a few days ago, when you answered the questions of the Prosecutor, on the 8th and 9th of July, on page 2 of his notes, you said the following. [In English] "They seized some tools and wire at his apartment." That's your apartment. "They accused him of using the wire to make bombs." [Interpretation] That's what you said to the Prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I also stated in my statement what Savo Cancarevic had told me and what he had asked me when I came to the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On several occasions in your statements you spoke about the fact that when you were imprisoned in Samac, detained in Samac, in various locations, that there were frequent power cuts, blackouts. Do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, I would ask him to state -- or to identify the places where he indicates that exists. I don't recall that either in his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Maybe I'm wrong, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about when you were detained in Samac in the TO. Do you have any personal knowledge of the fact that in that period, while you were in Samac, that the electricity would go out frequently?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pantelic, but you had mentioned that on several occasions the witness had said about frequent power cuts, blackouts, while he was imprisoned in several locations in Bosanski Samac, and Mr. Weiner asked for some reference to it. Maybe you could direct us to where you were talking about that, or rather, where you were reading it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, I'm checking with my colleagues, maybe it was an error in my notes. But I'll try to find out of his personal knowledge about the situation, and he answered that he is not aware about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have no problem with that, Your Honour. I just don't want it to be considered a prior inconsistent statement, because it doesn't exist here, or I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think Mr. Pantelic has moved on, because he has now asked the question directly to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was not my intention to catch the witness, you know, in this inconsistency, no, no, no. It was just a question with regard to the general conditions in the town, nothing special.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, then. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Subasic, can you please tell me: Do you have any personal knowledge of the fact that while you were in Samac during the combat operations, was the power supply -- the water supply also cut in the town? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge of the fact that Samac was shelled quite frequently at the time when you were detained there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often -- and can you tell us where the shells fell?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you where the shells landed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did hear the detonations and the explosions?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. Samac is a small town, so one can hear the explosions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: Since you mentioned to the Prosecutor that you saw my client, Mr. Blagoje Simic, in the TO courtyard, you mentioned that yesterday and today you gave some additional information, can you please remember if it was in the beginning of August or in mid-August 1992 when my client allegedly was seen in the courtyard of the TO building?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell you. I know that it was in the summer of 1992, but I can't remember the exact month, because while we were imprisoned there, we lost all sense of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at any rate, what you said to my colleague from the Prosecution, we could say you said that it was in August; right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, possibly. It was the only time, and it was for a very short period of time, perhaps five or ten minutes, not longer than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at the time when you allegedly saw him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was around you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other prisoners. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't remember any names?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that Kemal Mehinovic was there, Ado Dzakic, Ivan Dzakic. That's as much as I can remember now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Dr. Blagoje Simic alone when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was somebody else with him in a uniform, but I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: What was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a beard or a moustache?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since, as you say, before the war you only knew him by sight, do you allow for a possibility that you may have made a mistake, since you don't know him that well? Perhaps it was another person?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour. You're asking him to speculate: Do you allow for a possibility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. That is a proper question in cross-examination. Mr. Pantelic can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question related to your statement. Since you said that you knew him only by sight, which means not as well, you didn't know him so well, so perhaps you didn't have any specific knowledge of the way he actually looked. Do you allow for a possibility that may have been another person who looked like him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't allow that possibility. Because if I had made a mistake, other prisoners hadn't made the mistake, because, as I already said, I was not alone there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, yes, but I'm asking you first of all about your personal experience, since you don't know that man. How were you in a position to know that that was him? I mean you personally. We'll come to the other prisoners later, but now I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I already said, I knew him by sight. And when you say that, that means that I know that person very well, but we are not friends, we are not acquaintances. We know each other from the street, from passing each other in the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but just a minute ago, when I asked you to describe him, you told me you didn't remember, so I'm asking you now: Do you remember what Dr. Blagoje Simic physically looked like at the time when you knew him by sight, meaning before April 1992? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that, because it's been a long time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, in 2002, all of a sudden you do remember that. Have you talked to somebody in the meantime about that in preparation for the testimony here, or is it just a true recollection?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I simply remembered this. I haven't talked to anybody about it. I identified Mr. Simic correctly in 1998, and I identified him here correctly again. Another reason why I know Mr. Simic is that he was the head of the dialysis department, and my grandmother went to dialysis every other day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then, when you say that you went with your grandmother, are you trying to say that you accompanied your grandmother to the hospital and had an opportunity to see Dr. Simic there?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes I went with her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that you identified him in 1998. In what way did you do that? Were you given photographs?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the investigators from the Prosecution talked to me, I had to identify persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, when you looked at the defendants present here in this videolink, you basically recognised Dr. Simic, just as you did in 1998, when you were given his photograph; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you tense about something? Should we take a break or can we continue?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not tense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he looked the same in 1998, just as he looks now; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I think you've dealt with this identification problem sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions and I'm finished, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned that you followed something on Internet. Did you follow the trials here in The Hague on Internet?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I followed trials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your 1998 statement you never mentioned the presence of Dr. Blagoje Simic in the TO; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. If I didn't mention it, then probably it was because nobody asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 8th and 9th of July, you said the following to the Prosecution, on page 1. When you spoke about Blagoje Simic, you said you knew him only by sight and that you remember seeing him during the war. You said the following to the Prosecution: [In English] "[Previous translation continues]... occasions while the witness was being detained he saw the defendant in the courtyard of the TO." [Interpretation] Do you remember saying this to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that I stated that I had seen him on two occasions. I saw him only once, and quite briefly at that, five to ten minutes only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, bearing in mind that you did not mention him in your 1998 statement, bearing in mind that you don't remember what he looked like in 1992 and in 1998, except for the fact that you saw him just now, and in view of the fact that there are inconsistencies in your statements given to the Prosecution, and also bearing in mind what you told us just now, I'm asking you: What is your motive for not saying the truth and claiming that my client, Blagoje Simic, went to the TO? Who made you, who induced you to say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's a speech. That's not a question, Your Honour, that's argumentative. If he wants to break that up and ask separate questions, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. If you're challenging the witness on this, you can go ahead and do it, but break it down, as Mr. Weiner has said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I'm asking you now, Mr. Subasic: Since my client claims that he never visited the TO building, who suggested to you that you should mention him now, in 2002, ten years after the events in Samac and after several contacts you had with the Prosecution? Please give me the name. Is it somebody from the Prosecution or some of the people who had are living in the same town with you now?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me to say this. I don't see anything bad about this. Many people came to the TO building. I never said that Blagoje Simic mistreated anybody there. Perhaps he came just out of curiosity there. I don't know what the reason was. And I don't know why is he objecting to the fact that I mention seeing him there when in fact I did see him there. I would understand it if I had stated that he mistreated or beat somebody, but I didn't say anything of the sort. I simply said that I saw him briefly, for some five or ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Subasic, you told us you did not remember what he looked like in 1992, when you went to the dialysis department with your grandmother; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please repeat the question. You are talking too loud, so I can't understand what you're saying. I don't think there is any reason for you to raise your voice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I will repeat my question. You told us here that you did not remember what Dr. Blagoje Simic looked like in 1992, when you went with your grandmother to the dialysis centre. That's what you said to us just now: You don't remember.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it was in 1992, and it is true that I don't remember what he looked like. A lot of time has passed in the meantime, and I simply did not retain this. I don't remember what people who are much closer to me looked like. Ten years have passed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also do not remember what he looked like when you allegedly identified him in 1998, when urged by the Prosecution. You don't remember that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that, Your Honour. I have no problem with him asking what he looked like, even it's the second or third time he's asked it, but the final phrase I'd ask be stricken: "When urged by the Prosecution."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. There is no evidence to that effect, Mr. Pantelic. And I think I'll stop you. We've gone around this. You've put all the questions, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: One final question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. That's -- on another topic. The final question on another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, in 1998 you stated that your wife did not have a work obligation. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. She did not have a work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she tell you that the reason behind that was that she had minor children?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife herself was a minor, and we had a baby, two-month-old baby, when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did she tell you that that was the reason that she did not have a work obligation?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She did not know the reason for not having a work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour. I've finished with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Next counsel. Cross-examined by Mr. Krgovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Subasic. My name is Dragan Krgovic, I am an attorney representing Mr. Miroslav Tadic, and on behalf of him, I will be putting questions to you. I want to pick it up where you left it off with my colleague Pantelic, but, however, your answer was not recorded in the transcript. Your answer to the question regarding shelling of Samac. While you were in Samac, how frequent were these shellings?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I know there were shellings, but I can't tell you how frequent they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they daily, monthly, weekly?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember, and I wouldn't like to speculate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another thing I wanted to ask you is this: Yesterday you mentioned serving your mandatory military service. You said that you served in Sarajevo in 1989, in anti-aircraft unit. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: After completing your military service, you had your wartime assignment, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have a wartime assignment; at least, nobody informed me of this. As far as I know, I didn't have one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After completing your military service, did you report to the secretariat for defence, or the military office?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your military booklet, did they record your wartime assignment, military assignment in the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did not, but I can't claim with certainty. Perhaps they did. I simply don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive call-ups to attend military exercises?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any summons to go and be issued some equipment or be -- or to have your name entered into some military records?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you worked as a watchman in Mebos. You worked in the security?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had a stepped-up security, and several of us workers who had previously worked in the manufacturing process came to help the regular watchman, or the receptionist, and we worked as security guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: When were you assigned to do this?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in November or December of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please: At the time you were issued with a uniform?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not issued with a uniform. I worked in my civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you did not have any type of uniform as a security officer?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, please: You had a pistol that you received at work, your service pistol?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, can you try to avoid repeating evidence given in chief, please, and simply go to your questions. You see the arrangement with this witness is quite expensive, so if you can -- we can cut down on time as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply wanted to lay the ground for my next question, Your Honour, but I will try to proceed directly to the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, did you have a permit for your pistol?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only within the company's compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who issued that permit to you?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the company, Mebos company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that at the time, only the SUP was authorised to issue weapon permits?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, and I think that Mebos must have requested this permit from the SUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not receive a permit issued by the SUP to carry a weapon?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you still had that pistol even when you went home, meaning outside of the factory compound?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did not have a permit?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not have permit, but a lot of people carried weapons at that time without a permit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell me who else carried weapons without permits?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Simo Zaric, Mr. Miroslav Tadic. Did they have permits to carry automatic weapons? I don't know. Where can one obtain such permits?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether your neighbour, Dedo Halilovic, had a permit for an automatic weapon?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I never saw him carrying an automatic weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know that your neighbour, Dedo Halilovic, also possessed an automatic weapon called Kalashnikov?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you socialise with him?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not particularly. We knew each other by sight, we greeted each other, but we were not very close friends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His name is Dervis Halilovic, Dedo is his nickname; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably it is. I know him by his nickname, Dedo, and I know his last name is Halilovic, but I couldn't tell you his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he had also a nickname, Gusak?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us me, Mr. Subasic, who was your immediate superior while you were in the security at Mebos?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think his last name was Sejdinovic. I don't know his first name. I don't remember his first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because yesterday, when asked by the Prosecutor about the fact that your supervisor had told you to go and take a rest, you told us that your supervisor was a Serb, so what is it?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't my director or my immediate superior who came and told me this. I think that several guys came, one from Crkvina and one from another place, came and told me that I wasn't needed there any more, that I should go home, and if they should need me, they would come and get me. Both of them were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to see your immediate supervisor to inquire about whether there is any need for you to come to work?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that while you worked as a security guard, after April 17th, people of Serb ethnicity would come to the Mebos company and drive away the goods from there. Can you tell me whether you took any steps to prevent these people from taking away the goods manufactured at the company?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take any steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you inform anybody of this?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I called the police. I told them about that. They told me that they would send somebody regarding this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you talk with in the police?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the employee's name, the one who answered the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will switch to another topic. You said that you went to Cafe AS several times. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that members of all three ethnic communities frequented that cafe, all three ethnic communities populating Samac?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Ibrahim Salkic went to that cafe?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I simply said that I visited that cafe several times. I can't tell you who else was there. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did you visit that cafe with?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I went alone. That cafe was on my way to my apartment, so I think I went there alone. I can't even remember whether I had a drink there or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what the interior of that cafe looked like?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that the bar was to the right, but I couldn't give you any more details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, during your testimony yesterday, on page 37, you said that the night between 16th and 17th of April, 1992, you spent at home and that you went outside at about 6.00 or 6.30. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that afterwards you went to your grandmother's, where you spent some 45 minutes?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you return back home?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps around 7.15 or 7.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That morning?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 39, you said that late in the afternoon on the 17th of April, you saw Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric in front of your building. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement of the 3rd of May, 1998, on page 3,. "When on the following morning I looked out of my window, I saw many soldiers going from house to house. It looked to me as if they were searching for weapons. I also saw Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric sitting on the same military vehicle." Do you remember stating that to the Prosecutor in your interview on the 25th of April and 3rd of May, 1998?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A few days ago, when you discussed with the Prosecutor some things, the Prosecutor's notes reflect you as stating that in the late morning or early afternoon, you saw Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric in front of your building. So now I'm curious about this inconsistency in your statement.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, can you recollect now: When did you see Miroslav Tadic and Simo Zaric exactly? I'm interested both in the date and the time of the day.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you: That was ten years ago. I can't tell you exactly, but it was in the afternoon, on the first day when Samac was attacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, isn't that right that you cannot be specific about the time when you allegedly saw Simo Zaric and Miroslav Tadic because you were not at home that entire day on the 17th of April? Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, let's clear something. Please tell the Trial Chamber: At the time you lived together with your mother Bahrija; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she must have told you, since you said yourself she told you a lot of things about what was happening in Samac, that she was very much worried about you throughout the night and day because you only arrived at home -- you arrived home on the 18th at 5.00 in the morning?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where you get this information, but that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That morning, your mother went out of the house and went to visit her grandmother and went looking for you around Samac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, are you aware of the fact that your mother had spoken to the investigators of the OTP practically on the same day or the day after?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, are you aware of the fact that your mother stated to the investigators the following: "I went out of the house -- I went out of the house and then I went to sleep."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object. They're trying to question him based on what his mother said, and it's not as inconsistent. He's out at 6.30 in the morning, his mother is at home, she doesn't see him, she goes out looking for him. It's consistent with his testimony, but they're trying to impeach him with a statement made by his mother in 19 -- I'll get the exact date. It says dates of interview 2 May, 1950. I think they mean 1998, but I'm not -- they've got the wrong date on the statement. It's May 2nd. It says 1950, but I know the interview wasn't in 1950.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I'm trying to impeach this witness, but I'm also merely asking this witness whether he is aware of the fact that his mother stated the following, and whether she shared with him what she had told the investigators. And I'm merely trying to investigate whether the witness discussed this with his mother. We had the same situation with Esad Dagovic and his father. So I'm not confronting him with the statement of another witness, nor am I asking him to comment upon it. I'm merely asking him about his personal knowledge of what his mother had said. That's a legitimate way to conduct an examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I discussed this with my mother, but I don't remember her stating that. I really don't know what she stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've got no objection if he wants to ask him about his discussions that this witness had with his mother, number one. Number two, however, the Esad Dagovic situation was much different. There was a report which had never been disclosed, and I think the Court made a special ruling based on that. He can do this, ask, you know, what discussions he had with his mother in relation to the issue of bias or if it is a relevant issue. However, they're trying to impeach with the statement of one versus the other. So far we haven't allowed that to be done. But actually, it's not even -- he can do it. It's not even inconsistent. Because when the mother gets the uncle's house, which are both in the same compound, he says it's there. There's no inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not quoting from the statement. I'm merely asking the witness whether he's aware of the fact that his mother had said this and that, and whether she had done this or that. I'm not quoting from the statement. I'm not trying to tender it into evidence. I'm not confronting the witness with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, are you aware of the fact -- or rather, did your mother tell you that she was worried about you because you were out the whole night, since you left home at 10.00 a.m., or rather, 10.00 p.m. - I'm sorry - on the 16th of April, and that she said that at 7.00 a.m. she went into town looking for you, that she didn't find you, that she went to her mother's place, didn't find you there either, and then she returned home, and then a neighbour told her that you were safe and that she should not worry, and that you came home at 5.00 a.m. on the 18th of April and that she was unable to sleep? Did your mother tell you about that?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that right? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Once again, he's trying to impeach. Just what he said he wasn't going to do, he's doing now he's trying to impeach one witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Krgovic. I wonder whether I could just ask the witness a small question. I wonder whether you could tell us: During this time period in question that Mr. Krgovic is discussing, where your wife and two-month-old baby were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the apartment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, did your mother tell you that she had given a statement to the investigators of the Tribunal in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, she did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she tell you that what I just told you, that she stated that to the investigators of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't tell me that. We didn't discuss it in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Subasic, did you, together with your mother, answer the questions asked by the Prosecutor a week ago?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did it separately. My mother didn't speak to the Prosecutors a week ago. They merely asked a few short questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was she present when you spoke with the Prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: HASAN SUBASIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
